label: prop:linear-chain-bond-count
title: The jet-filtration multiplicity is the linear-chain bond count $M_n = n-1$
html:
Proposition (bond-count multiplicity). The canonical atomic braid is a linear chain of A nucleon blocks (consecutive blocks joined by a single inter-nucleon crossing). Consequently, in the body-order (jet-filtration) binding conj:binding-manybody-eq-jet-filtration,

  • the number of consecutive n-nucleon sub-clusters is A-n+1, and
  • each n-nucleon sub-chain carries exactly n-1 inter-nucleon bonds,

so the body-order multiplicity is the bond count M_n = n-1. The aggregate bond-weighted cluster measure of the A-chain is the tetrahedral (binomial) number

  \sum_{n=2}^{A} (A-n+1)\,(n-1)
  \;=\; \binom{A+1}{3}
  \;=\; \frac{(A-1)\,A\,(A+1)}{6}.

Reindexed by k = n-1 this is \sum_{k=0}^{A-1}(A-k)\,k, and the identity follows by induction on A.

The multiplicity M_n = n-1 fixes the per-body-order weight of the θ_λ residue w_n(K) = M_n\,\mathrm{Vol}_n(K) with no fitted constant — the count is the inter-nucleon bond number of the derived linear chain, and \mathrm{Vol}_n(K) is the hyperbolic volume of the n-body sub-link (the isospin carrier).

Scope. Only the combinatorial multiplicity is asserted here. The binding magnitude B(K) = \mathfrak{m}_e \sum_{n} M_n\,\mathrm{Vol}_n(K) — which reproduces the tritium binding to \approx 0.16\% with no fit (theta_mn_bondcount_linearchain.py) — is an empirical consequence that also multiplies in the topological link volumes and the electron scale \mathfrak{m}_e; it is not part of this proposition, and it carries a \sim 3\% mirror-pair residual plus a deuteron (\mathrm{Vol}=0 Hopf) exception.
